answer: Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 2 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. Histories are stored in bridge, checked in summit, and walnut makes public each void. A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. The per-identity price is 75 dollars, and it is forfeited outright on the first bad verdict. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
